table_title: List buildings whose architectural height (per Wikipedia's `List of tallest buildings` master ranking) is at least 500 metres, with city, country, that architectural height, and the Year cell from the master table. As of 2026 master accessed 2026-05-18: 11 rows. Scope = the master article's stated scope clause: 'completed and architecturally topped out as of 2026'. Sort = Architectural Height DESC primary; Year ASC secondary tiebreak at the 530 m tie between Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre (2016) and Tianjin CTF Finance Centre (2019); Building ASC final tiebreak.
db_analog: SELECT b.building, b.city, b.country, b.architectural_height_m, b.year FROM tallest_buildings_topped_out_2026 b WHERE b.architectural_height_m >= 500 ORDER BY b.architectural_height_m DESC, b.year ASC, b.building ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `List of tallest buildings` master article (roles = [universe, ranking, value]: scope-defines the building universe via the article's verbatim scope clause, supplies the architectural-height ranking, supplies Building / City / Country / Architectural Height (m) / Year cells verbatim from the main ranking table), accessed 2026-05-18. source_count = 1 registered. The master article's table is canonically titled 'completed and architecturally topped out' — per the article's introduction 'As of 2026, this list includes all 98 buildings (completed and architecturally topped out) that reach a height of 350 m (1,150 ft) or more'. The 500 m staged threshold is a curator-chosen pragmatic deterministic cutoff (NOT a CTBUH-defined named tier — CTBUH's canonical named thresholds are supertall ≥ 300 m and megatall ≥ 600 m; 500 m sits between those tiers as an honest round-number cutoff that yields 11 rows). temporal_sensitivity = medium because the active construction pipeline (Jeddah Tower at 1000 m+ under construction; multiple ≥ 500 m projects in pipeline) means the 11-row universe is stable over benchmark timescales but not stable over multi-year horizons. The master article's published list is regularly updated; year-anchor = master accessed 2026-05-18. Per-row cells are verbatim from the master table for Building + City + Country + Architectural Height (m); Year is the master's 'Year' column verbatim (the master gives 'Year' not 'Opening Year' or 'Completion Year'). The '≥ 500 m architectural-height threshold' rule is deterministic; no curator-judgment selection beyond the round-number cutoff. The next row immediately below the threshold is Shanghai World Financial Center at 492 m — comfortably below 500 m; no boundary ambiguity. CITIC Tower (also commonly known as China Zun) is a single building; the master uses 'CITIC Tower' as the canonical name.
_extraction_notes: Comparative instance — single-table threshold filter (Architectural Height ≥ 500 m) over the Wikipedia `List of tallest buildings` master ranking. PIVOT from `roller_coasters_taller_than_100_meters` after cycle-0 source exploration on 2026-05-18 found (a) the proposed roller-coaster source article `List of roller coasters taller than 100 metres` does not exist (404 — durable), (b) the available Wikipedia coaster-height sources consulted at cycle-0 time did not appear to support a > 100 m universe of ≥ 10 rows under any deterministic source-defined framing (exact row counts + section-framing wording from cycle-0 are time-anchored to 2026-05-18 and not re-asserted as live state), (c) Wikipedia's named coaster height categories (hyper ≥ 61 m, giga ≥ 91 m, strata ≥ 122 m) do not cleanly land at 100 m. Audit-cycle-1 design review issued 6 required amendments + per-question recommendations, all incorporated: (1) universe pinned to exactly 11 rows (NOT 11-13); CITIC Tower and China Zun are the same building counted once; the 530 m tie is Guangzhou CTF + Tianjin CTF only; (2) 500 m is NOT described as a CTBUH-defined tier — instead documented as a curator-chosen pragmatic deterministic cutoff between supertall ≥ 300 m and megatall ≥ 600 m; (3) source's actual scope clause used verbatim: 'completed and architecturally topped out as of 2026' (NOT 'completed-and-opened only' which would require a different source or curator override); (4) Year column staged as 'Year' verbatim per master (NOT 'Opening Year' which was not source-faithful); (5) entity class = engineered-structures/buildings EXISTING fine-class — NOT a new `skyscrapers` fine-class, per the locked duplicate-detection policy: the answer entity is still a building; a 500 m filter changes the query scope, not the underlying entity class; (6) ID renamed from `skyscrapers_taller_than_500_meters_worldwide` (which implied > 500) to `skyscrapers_at_least_500_meters_worldwide` (which matches the ≥ 500 predicate). Brings `comparative` from gap 2 (3 of 5: countries_with_more_than_5_fields_medalists + tennis_players_with_more_than_5_grand_slam_singles_titles + largest_asteroids_with_geometric_mean_diameter_above_250_km) to **gap 1 (4 of 5)** — one more saturates as the 11th fully-cleared category. Technology/Civil Engineering EXISTING subdomain (joining `notable_bridges_by_main_span` + `worlds_tallest_dams_by_structural_height`). engineered-structures/buildings EXISTING fine-class (held by `trial_union_4`) — this instance is a 2nd buildings-keyed staged instance, NOT a NEW fine-class. Schema: 5 cols (Building PK + City + Country + Architectural Height (m) + Year). Architectural Height is the ranking attribute that defines row selection (same precedent as Geometric Mean Diameter in asteroids + Atomic Number in periodic-table-groups + Apparent Magnitude in zodiac-stars). Sort: Architectural Height DESC primary; Year ASC secondary tiebreak at the 530 m tie (Guangzhou CTF 2016 → Tianjin CTF 2019); Building ASC final tiebreak (not triggered for the current 11-row universe). claim_type = `source_defined` — single-master deterministic-numeric-threshold pattern (analogous to asteroids ≥ 250 km, rivers > 1000 km, films winning ≥ 8 Oscars). Universe scope clause + ranking rule + value cells all from one master; curator-chosen 500 m threshold is the only curator-judgment input, and it is documented as such. Year-anchor: master accessed 2026-05-18; temporal_sensitivity=medium because the construction pipeline is active. Audit-cycle-1 per-question recommendations applied: (Q1) architectural height NOT tip; (Q2) master's completed-and-topped-out scope; (Q3) year-anchor as-of-2026 master accessed 2026-05-18; (Q4) Technology/Civil Engineering domain; (Q5) City + Country cells master-verbatim; (Q6) universe = exactly 11 rows + boundary = Shanghai World Financial Center 492 m; (Q7) ≥ 500 m kept as pragmatic deterministic cutoff with ≥ 600 m (4 rows, below gate) + ≥ 400 m (much broader) alternatives noted; (Q8) deterministic-universe-rule preference satisfied (SQL-WHERE = `architectural_height_meters >= 500`).
